assumptions: refunds and users are the sensitive tables to audit; the customer did not name tables
the refund approval endpoint is the approval control to record
policies stay advisory; making them blocking is the owner's choice
new objects need no guid line; the dry run did not complain
confusions: the recipe audit_changes says to tag the audited tables and name them by exact name in each rule, but the tag step is not spelled out in the template (which tag, and whether the table needs it), so I used exact table names in when.tables and skipped tagging

the skill says an active policy that cannot run makes the branch gates unavailable, but a policy whose rule names a function not yet on the branch does not say whether it will run after push; the dry run did not show it
object.statement_required's when.tables for db.del: the catalogue does not say whether db.bulk.delete is covered by db.del, so my AUDIT-001 delete rule may miss bulk deletes
XanoScript for a policy file: whether a rule with no params needs an empty params line or may omit params was not shown in the skill; I omitted it for test.assertion_required and parse accepted it
wished_for: a recipe or template for audit of a named set of tables, as a single policy, rather than three statement-specific rules
a template for access reviews that is honest about being process-only, with the evidence it can give (login required, audit trail present)
a statement that the dry run checks whether each rule has an object to judge, not only whether names exist
why_confidence: The audit trail, login requirement and test coverage are real and checkable, and the dry run is clean. But access reviews and change approvals are process controls no check can see, and the audit covers only refunds and users, so the auditor will still need evidence outside the workspace. I did not evaluate the policies, so I do not know what they will flag.
